source.title: Belfast News-Letter, 20 September 1946, p. 3 ("Fermanagh nominations")
source.publisher: Belfast News-Letter (via the Irish Newspaper Archives)
source.check: Two nominations were received, Reihill and Anthony Ruddy, both Nationalists; the Impartial Reporter of 26 September records that Ruddy then withdrew

note: Triennial election, polled Thursday 3 October 1946. Nominations closed on 19 September and the Belfast News-Letter of 20 September, p. 3, reported contests in two divisions: Garrison (Patrick Casey, N., and Hamilton Scott, U.) and Irvinestown (Patrick Reihill, N., the retiring councillor, and Anthony Ruddy, N.). The Impartial Reporter of 26 September, p. 5, then records that Ruddy withdrew, so Reihill was returned unopposed and Garrison was the only poll. Garrison was won by the Nationalist (Casey 139, Scott 129). The same report lists nine changes among the uncontested seats — Belleek, Brookhill, Churchill, Clonelly, Ederney, Innismacsaint, Kesh, Killadeas and Milltown — and the remaining members are recorded where a selection list or a report of the new council's meetings names them. Belleek is one of the district's nineteen divisions (Kingsley, 'James Cooper and the Defence of Fermanagh's Electoral Arrangements 1923-1924', Table 6) but is absent from the 1939 return. Castlecaldwell: the death of Mr. Henry McBride was reported in August 1947 (Fermanagh Herald, 9 August 1947, p. 3); Anthony Ruddy was the outgoing member in 1949; how the vacancy was filled was not found. Returned unopposed on Mr. Ruddy's withdrawal. Returned unopposed.
